definitions.definition: Ttor = reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi); spatial products and integrals are on this domain.
For an integrable periodic f, Fourier(f)(k)=hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x) exp(-i*k*x) dx; the transform extends to distributions by duality.

For every real s, H^s(Ttor) is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_(k in Z) <k>^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2, <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). Negative spaces are interpreted as distributions. Homogeneous norms on zero-mean distributions are ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_(k!=0)|k|^(2*s)|hat f(k)|^2. Real means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0.

L2=H^0(Ttor), with ||f||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-1) integral |f|^2 dx. More generally L^p uses the same normalized measure; L^infinity is essential supremum. Sequence ell^2 uses counting measure on Z (or Z\{0} when specified). Time suprema use continuous representatives; derivative norms are essential suprema.

definitions.type: Airy group indexed by real time

definitions.definition: P0(f)=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
Pnz=I-P0, denoted P in the supplied proof. Fourier projections P_leq(N) and P_gt(N) retain |k|<=N and |k|>N respectively, for N>=0.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has Fourier multiplier (i*k)^(-1) at nonzero integer k and zero at k=0. Dinv2=(Dinv)^2 is denoted D^(-2).

definitions.type: quadratic update family for positive timestep
definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L2, Ftau(f)=(1/6)*Pnz[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)*S_tau Pnz[(Dinv f)^2].

definitions.type: cubic update family for positive timestep
definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L2, Htau(f)=(1/3)*Pnz[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv Ftau(f)]+(tau/9)*(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)*[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))*[S_(tau-s) Dinv2[(S_(s-tau) Dinv2 Ftau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Brackets mean the value at tau minus the value at zero. All products are spatial products.

For every positive tau, Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f) on mean-zero L2 data. Given such tau, mean-zero u0 in L2 and an integer L>=1, set t_n=n*tau, u^0=u0 and u^(n+1)=Psi_tau(u^n) for 0<=n<L; write v^n=S_(-t_n)u^n. For the target with T>0, specialize tau=T/L. There is no spatial cutoff.
Bop_t(f,g)=S_(-t)*partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)], initially for smooth periodic functions and by distributional product for L2 inputs.
Jop_t(f,g)=S_(-t) Pnz[(S_t Dinv f)(S_t Dinv g)].

For a time interval I=[a,b], Cop_I(f,g,h)=integral_a^b S_(-t) Pnz{Pnz[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))} dt. Initially this is defined for smooth inputs; the continuous extensions in the source estimates are meant when used for rough inputs.

output.statement: S_t is an isometry on every H^s and preserves real functions and zero mean; Fourier projections contract these norms. For mean-zero L2 inputs, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||Bop_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||Jop_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2 and ||Jop_t(A,B)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||B||_2, uniformly in t. For arbitrary L2 F,G, ||Dinv Pnz(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2. H^1 embeds continuously into L^infinity and satisfies ||AB||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||B||_(H^1). For time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b Bop_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[Jop_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[Jop_t(f',g)+Jop_t(f,g')]dt. Also Jop is symmetric and integral_I Jop_t(Bop_t(f,g),h)dt=Cop_I(f,g,h). These identities hold piecewise in time and add across adjoining steps with their common endpoints. For every fixed tau>0, Ftau:L2_zero->H^1 and Psi_tau:L2_zero->L2_zero are continuous polynomial maps, preserve reality, and map smooth data to smooth data; all finite iterates are therefore well defined and continuous in L2.

argument.text: All claims in this paragraph are universally quantified over the indicated functions and real times. S_t has multiplier of modulus one, conjugate-compatible at k and -k, and does not mix frequencies, proving the isometry, reality, mean and projection assertions. For mean-zero f, Cauchy–Schwarz gives ||Dinv f||_infinity<= (sum_(k!=0)k^(-2))^(1/2)||f||_2 and ||Dinv f||_(H^1)<=sqrt(2)||f||_2. For arbitrary A in H^1 its Fourier ell1 norm is bounded by (sum_k<k>^(-2))^(1/2)||A||_(H^1), giving H^1->L^infinity. The product rule and this embedding give ||AB||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||B||_(H^1). Apply this to the two inverse derivatives in Jop for its H^1 bound. Bounding Dinv B in L^infinity and Dinv A in L2 gives the asymmetric Jop bound.

produces.statement: For every real t, S_t is an isometry on every H^s, preserves reality and zero mean, and Fourier projections contract H^s norms. For mean-zero f in L2, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2. For A,B in H^1, ||A||_infinity<=C||A||_(H^1) and ||AB||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||B||_(H^1). For mean-zero L2 f,g, ||Jop_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2; for mean-zero A,B with Dinv A in L2 and B in L2, ||Jop_t(A,B)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||B||_2.

argument.text: For any L2 F,G the coefficient of FG has absolute value at most ||F||_2||G||_2 by Cauchy–Schwarz in the convolution. Thus the squared H^(-pstar) norm of Bop_t(f,g) is <=||f||_2^2||g||_2^2 sum_(k!=0)k^2<k>^(-2*pstar), a finite sum because pstar=23/14>3/2. The same coefficient bound with sum_(k!=0)k^(-2) gives ||Dinv Pnz(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, <k>^(-pstar)<=|k|^(-1), proving ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2. Density extends all these continuous product bounds from polynomials; the product FG is an L1 function and Fourier convolution agrees with it by L2 approximation and the L1 product estimate.

produces.statement: For mean-zero L2 f,g, ||Bop_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For L2 F,G, ||Dinv Pnz(FG)||_2<=C||F||_2||G||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2. Constants are uniform in real t.

argument.text: For any time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero f,g, the k!=0 coefficient of Jop_t(f,g) is sum_(a+b=k) exp(-i*t*3*k*a*b)*(i*a)^(-1)*(i*b)^(-1)*hat f(a)*hat g(b). Differentiating its phase produces 3*i*k, so partial_t Jop_t(f,g)=3 Bop_t(f,g)+Jop_t(f',g)+Jop_t(f,g'). Smooth Fourier series and all derivatives here are absolutely convergent. Integrating yields the stated normal-form identity, with both endpoints. Symmetry follows from the product. Since Dinv partial_x=Pnz, substitution gives Jop_t(Bop_t(f,g),h)=S_(-t)Pnz{Pnz[(S_t f)(S_t g)]*(S_t Dinv h)}, whose integral is Cop. For piecewise smooth functions apply on each smooth time piece and add; continuous endpoint values telescope.

produces.statement: For smooth mean-zero f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b Bop_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[Jop_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b(Jop_t(f',g)+Jop_t(f,g'))dt. Jop_t(f,g)=Jop_t(g,f), and integral_I Jop_t(Bop_t(f,g),h)dt=Cop_I(f,g,h). Identities concatenate for continuous piecewise smooth inputs.

argument.text: For fixed tau>0, each term in Ftau is an H^1 product of inverse derivatives, hence a continuous quadratic L2->H^1 map by F001. In Htau the first term is again an H^1 product. The bilinear mean P0(f^2) is continuous by the L2 product bound, so the second term is continuous. Its third term is an H^1 cubic product followed by Dinv, and its fourth term is a product of Dinv2 Ftau(f) and Dinv f followed by Dinv2. All group factors preserve Sobolev norms and all coefficients, including tau^(-1), are finite for fixed tau. This proves L2 continuity. Pnz and inverse derivatives force zero mean except in the second term; that term is a scalar multiple of S_tau Dinv f and also has zero mean. Each operation preserves reality; smooth functions remain smooth under all these operations. The recurrence therefore has well-defined continuous finite iterates and preserves real mean-zero data.
